claim: Scientific conferences have an important role in the exchange of ideas and knowledge within the scientific community.
source: Scientific conferences have an important role in the exchange of ideas and knowledge within the scientific community.
evidence: This is a general statement about the role of conferences, representing established knowledge in the scientific community.

claim: Conferences provide early-career researchers with opportunities to make themselves known within their field of research.
source: Conferences also provide early-career researchers with opportunities to make themselves known within their field of research.
evidence: This is a general statement about conference benefits, representing established knowledge.

claim: The COVID-19 pandemic has brought traditional in-person conferences to a halt for the foreseeable future.
source: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has brought traditional in-person conferences to a halt for the foreseeable future, the growth of virtual conferences has highlighted many of the disadvantages associated with the in-person format and demonstrated the advantages of moving these events online.
evidence: This statement reflects the known impact of COVID-19 on conferences during the pandemic period.

claim: The growth of virtual conferences has highlighted many disadvantages associated with the in-person format.
source: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has brought traditional in-person conferences to a halt for the foreseeable future, the growth of virtual conferences has highlighted many of the disadvantages associated with the in-person format and demonstrated the advantages of moving these events online.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between virtual and in-person conferences presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Virtual conferences are more inclusive than in-person conferences.
source: Here, based on data from in-person and virtual conferences in a range of subjects, we describe how virtual conferences are more inclusive, more affordable, less time-consuming and more accessible worldwide, especially for early-career researchers.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the figures showing increased participation from diverse groups.

claim: Virtual conferences are more affordable than in-person conferences.
source: Here, based on data from in-person and virtual conferences in a range of subjects, we describe how virtual conferences are more inclusive, more affordable, less time-consuming and more accessible worldwide, especially for early-career researchers.
evidence: This claim is supported by data and discussion about registration fees throughout the manuscript.

claim: Virtual conferences are less time-consuming than in-person conferences.
source: Here, based on data from in-person and virtual conferences in a range of subjects, we describe how virtual conferences are more inclusive, more affordable, less time-consuming and more accessible worldwide, especially for early-career researchers.
evidence: This is inferred from the elimination of travel time and the ability to attend asynchronously.

claim: Virtual conferences are more accessible worldwide than in-person conferences.
source: Here, based on data from in-person and virtual conferences in a range of subjects, we describe how virtual conferences are more inclusive, more affordable, less time-consuming and more accessible worldwide, especially for early-career researchers.
evidence: This is supported by data showing increased international participation in virtual conferences.

claim: Virtual conferences are especially beneficial for early-career researchers.
source: Here, based on data from in-person and virtual conferences in a range of subjects, we describe how virtual conferences are more inclusive, more affordable, less time-consuming and more accessible worldwide, especially for early-career researchers.

claim: In-person conferences exacerbate inequalities in academic communities.

source: Since virtual meetings have lower or no registration fees, they are open to a much wider variety of researchers.

claim: Online conferences have particularly increased participation of researchers from countries with low-to-middle income economies.
